Three declarations together state Lemma B.4: exists_reference_bounds (order Λ, C, t_1; the bounds (B.23) on [0,110]×[-1,1], strict, with c = 1/4), reference_first_gt_three (p_1 > 3 on [100,110]) and uniform_reference_quantities (the closing C^k sentence, for all C ≥ 1 and all 2δ < log(41/40)). Every conclusion is at least as strong as the paper's, so the verdict stays OK. findings.summary: The headline structure gives p_{1,r} > 3 only at X = 100. The paper's interval X_b ≤ X ≤ X_i is stated by a separate theorem, reference_first_gt_three, derived from the same ReferenceBoundsOnHold.

exists_reference_bounds assumes SmallParameters (h ≤ 1/1000, j ≤ 1/1000), narrower than p.144's printed 0<h≤10^-2 and 0<j_0≤.05. The paper's own smallness order puts its fixed parameters inside the Lean range.

The closing uniform-C^k sentence is not in the headline theorem. uniform_reference_quantities states it, more strongly, with its own threshold stabilityScale ≤ Λ. The headline docstring cites a stale 'Lemma 5.2'.

Lean's reference continuation damps slopes with Mathlib's Real.smoothTransition (glue exp(-1/x)), not the paper's step σ of (A.5) (glue exp(-1/y²)), which the repo defines separately as OutgoingSchedule.sigma. The bounds are proved for a different (φ_r, U_r).
